title: A Real Village Frozen in the 1600s
summary: A walk through Culross, Fife: Culross Palace, the Townhouse, the Mercat Cross, the Biscuit Cafe, Tanhouse Brae and the old Boat House, plus Outlander's Cranesmuir, little changed in 400 years.

title: The Boy Who Invented the Propeller
summary: A real, still-working fishing harbour beneath the ruins of Dunbar Castle, where creel boats work from the quay. Robert Wilson, born in a cottage here in 1803, had a screw propeller model shown to the Earl of Lauderdale in 1827, and a Highland Society test at Leith followed in 1828 — the Royal Navy turned him down, and history mostly forgot him too. Today there's a monument on the quay, a seafood stall called Nauti (check its opening days), and a long stone wall hung with buoys, lifebelts and painted boat name boards.

title: The World's Smallest Lighthouse
summary: Tucked under the shadow of the Forth Bridge sits a tiny working light tower — usually dated to 1817, dark for decades, and lit again since 2010. It's a genuine curiosity most people driving straight past never notice.

title: The Park a Billionaire Gave Away
summary: According to the Carnegie Trust, Andrew Carnegie was banned from the private grounds of Pittencrieff Estate as a boy. Decades later, having become one of the richest men in the world, he bought the entire estate — and gave it to a trust for the people of Dunfermline. Today it's about 76 acres of parkland and ruins, still free to everyone.

title: The Fort That Never Fired a Shot
summary: A listed red-sandstone gun battery on Lamer Island, Dunbar Harbour, with sixteen gun embrasures originally. Listed as built in 1781, though the site's own board gives the Napoleonic period, and said never to have fired in anger.

title: No Longer a Working Light
summary: A walk to Barns Ness Lighthouse, East Lothian: a Stevenson tower built in 1899–1901, decommissioned in 2005, then sold to the cement company next door, on a protected coast (SSSI).

title: The Harbour Village Painted in Colour
summary: A working East Neuk fishing harbour, boats still coming in daily, wrapped around a decades-old arts festival and murals of puffins and seals. Real fishing village, real art trail, one of Fife's most photographed corners.

title: Limekilns, Fife | A Path Made of Memories
summary: A medieval port for Dunfermline Abbey, now with boats on moorings, and Beacon Way, a path of engraved stones on the pier that ends on a question.

title: The Fishwives' Harbour | Newhaven, Edinburgh
summary: A harbour district of Edinburgh, reached by tram: the 1896 Fishmarket, two lighthouses, and the fishwives photographed by Hill and Adamson in the 1840s.

title: Lime Kilns by the Forth | Charlestown, Fife
summary: Lime kilns and a harbour on the Fife shore of the Forth, about 17 miles by road from Edinburgh Waverley. HES (Historic Environment Scotland) describes the Charlestown limekilns as “the largest group of limekilns in Scotland”.

title: Aberdour Harbour, Fife
summary: A tidal harbour on the Fife coast, 17.3 rail miles from Edinburgh.

title: Kirkcaldy War Memorial Gardens, Fife
summary: Kirkcaldy War Memorial Gardens, Fife. The bronze plaque on the cenotaph is dedicated to the men of Kirkcaldy who gave their lives in the Great War.
